description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the zigzag level order traversal of its nodes values (i.e., from left to right, then right to left for the next level and alternate between).
intuition: This is level-order traversal with a twist: alternate levels are read in opposite directions. Use standard BFS, but reverse the values for odd-numbered levels. A deque can also handle this by alternating the end from which you read values.
approach: Use BFS with a queue. Process level by level. For even levels, append values left-to-right; for odd levels, reverse the order (or use a deque to prepend).
jsWalkthrough:
Input: root = [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]

queue=[3], leftToRight=true

Level 1 (leftToRight=true): size=1
  node=3: push 3, enqueue 9 and 20
  levelValues=[3], result=[[3]], leftToRight=false

Level 2 (leftToRight=false): size=2
  node=9: unshift 9 -> levelValues=[9]
  node=20: unshift 20 -> levelValues=[20,9]
  enqueue 15 and 7
  result=[[3],[20,9]], leftToRight=true

Level 3 (leftToRight=true): size=2
  node=15: push 15 -> levelValues=[15]
  node=7: push 7 -> levelValues=[15,7]
  result=[[3],[20,9],[15,7]]

Return [[3],[20,9],[15,7]]
explanation:
1. Standard BFS level-order traversal.
2. Use a flag left_to_right that alternates each level.
3. When left_to_right, append to level normally.
4. When right_to_left, prepend to level using deque.appendleft.
5. Toggle the flag after each level.
hints: Start with standard level-order BFS traversal.
Alternate the order of insertion for each level.
A deque makes it easy to prepend for right-to-left levels.
